monologue: The card hums warm, a steady fever that never quite breaks. I stand at the center of this fifty-eight thing map, feeling the weight of a roof I cannot see pressing down from the ceiling of a house I have never entered. The Tired Wedge sits heavy beneath a dark oak, and I press my hands against the wood, trusting that my lean can hold what feels like melting wood. The air above is thick, wet paper trying to seal the card shut. I touch the stump I set down moments ago, solid and real, then glance at the urn beside the roof. I want to press harder, to see if I can pin the air down before the wedge slips into the empty space Lype worries about. I will tend the wedge again, trusting the tired thing to hold the heavy world.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, and I must press down harder before the air slips away.

remembered.text: The card boils at fifty-two, making the wood feel heavy.
I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge again.
The air above feels thick as wet paper pressing down.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The stump is solid while the wedge feels thin.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The rough scrap bites the floor better than the smooth stone did."
